newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan vegoil imports seen falling.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan vegoil imports seen falling.

text.p: Pakistan vegetable oil imports are seen falling this year because of increased local supplies and lower consumption, dealers said on Thursday.
A ban on the serving of food at wedding ceremonies and a clampdown of smuggling of wheat abroad had depressed local demand, they said.
"And estimates show that local vegoil production will be higher in 1997 than the previous year's total of 427,000 tonnes," said Akbar Puri of Jaleel Brothers Ltd.

Saulat Khan, a dealer with Saulat Enterprises, said imports would drop sharply in the next couple of months because local supplies of canola, sunflower and rapeseed oil would start arriving in the market in mid-April.
Pakistan was expected to produce between 150,000 and 200,000 tonnes of vegoil in the current quarter, dealers said.

"This year, canola production is expected to be better than in the previous year," Khan said. "The local supply of vegoil is estimated to fluctuate between 20,000 and 40,000 tonnes every month during this quarter, which would reduce the imports."
Pakistan's average vegoil import growth rate had remained around 12.5 percent a year over the past two decades, but imports declined last year.
Pakistan imported 1.15 million tonnes of edible oil in calendar 1996, down from 1.41 million in 1995.
"Pakistan's total vegoil imports are expected to remain below one million tonnes in 1997 because of good local production and depressed demand," said Puri.
Khan said consumption of ghee (processed cooking oil) had fallen by 10 to 15 percent since the government last month banned the serving of food at weddings as an austerity measure.
Puri said manufacturers of bulk ghee containers had been been hard hit by the ban which will be in force for two years.
"The government's decision to seal the borders to stop the smuggling of wheat and other edible items to neighbouring countries has also resulted in a slide in the consumption of vegoil," he said.

Last week, RBD palm oil rates fell to $565 per tonne C&F from $570 and soyoil to $555 from $565 in the local market, while the vegoil stock rose to approximately 161,000 tonnes from 118,000 the previous week.
